question: Under the provisions of which Article of the Indian Constitution, the President is empowered to constitute a Finance Commission at the expiration of every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President may consider necessary?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 280**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution empowers the **President** to constitute a **Finance Commission** at the expiration of every **fifth year** or at such earlier time as the President may consider necessary.
 
• The **Finance Commission is responsible for recommending the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States,** among other duties related to the financial relations between them.
 
• **This includes**:
 
 
• The allocation of net proceeds of taxes,
 
• The principles governing the grants-in-aid to States from the Union,
 
• The measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to meet its requirements.
 
 
 
• The Finance Commission **also advises **on any other matters related to financial relations between the Centre and the States, as referred to it by the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 281**:

 
 
• Article 281 specifies that the **President** must lay the **recommendations** made by the Finance Commission before both **Houses of Parliament** along with an explanatory note.
 
• This **ensures **that the recommendations are made public and are presented to the legislative bodies for consideration.
 
• This article **ensures transparency in the functioning of the Finance Commission and the presentation of its recommendations before the Parliament.**
 
 
 
• **​​Article 282:**
 
 
• Article 282 gives both the **Union government** and the **State governments** the **discretionary power** to make grants for any public purpose to any other government (Union or State) or authority.
 
• This article allows the Union and State governments to make grants for purposes not necessarily related to their specific jurisdiction, but for broader public welfare, thus supporting various developmental activities.
 
 
 
• **Article 283**:
 
 
• Article 283 deals with the **custody** of the **Consolidated Fund of India** and **State Funds**.
 
• It specifies that the funds should be held by the **President** (for the Union) or the **Governor** (for States), and details the responsibility of the Union and States in managing these funds.
 
• This article establishes the framework for proper management of the government’s accounts and financial resources, ensuring fiscal discipline.
